note: First judgement, 2026-10-24, by an independent auditor who authored none of these units. RFC 9774 Section 3: "Unless explicitly configured by a network operator to do otherwise (e.g., during a transition phase), BGP speakers:" ... "MUST use the "treat-as-withdraw" error handling behavior per [RFC7606] upon reception of BGP UPDATE messages containing AS_SETs or AS_CONFED_SETs in the AS_PATH or AS4_PATH [RFC6793]." The AS_PATH clause is enforced: TestValidateASPathRejectsSetSegments asserts exact TreatAsWithdraw, AttrCode 2 and the exact RFC 9774 Section 3 description for an AS_SET or AS_CONFED_SET first, middle, last or alone, at 2- and 4-octet width, and exact nil for seven set-free paths (sequence and confed-sequence mixes, empty); TestRFC9774ReceiveASSetTreatAsWithdraw drives Session.enforceRFC7606 on 2-octet eBGP, 4-octet eBGP and iBGP sessions, asserts no session error and exact TreatAsWithdraw for each set type, and exact None for a twin path with the matching sequence type in the set's place, so the verdict is bound to the segment type alone. TestRFC9774ReceiveASSetAcceptedByOperator (new positive tag, 745db0775d) proves the default through the real config entry: a peer parsed by parsePeerFromTree with no as-set leaf or with withdraw has AcceptASSet false and draws exact TreatAsWithdraw for AS_SET and AS_CONFED_SET in AS_PATH and for an AS_SET in AS4_PATH; its claim states only that and the body checks exactly that. Its accept rows are the operator exception the sentence itself allows, recorded as an uncounted deviation in rfc/short/rfc9774.md. WEAK on question 4, the AS4_PATH clause: among the tagged units it is proven only at positive polarity, for AS_SET only, and on a 2-octet session only. No tagged unit would go red if validateAS4PathAttr stopped being reached on a 4-octet session (validateAS4PathAttr's own doc says it rejects a set "on every session whatever the negotiated AS width"), if an AS_CONFED_SET in AS4_PATH were kept, or if a set-free AS4_PATH were over-withdrawn under the default policy. Those cases ARE asserted, exactly, by the untagged TestRFC9774ReceiveAS4PathSetTreatAsWithdraw (both set types, 2- and 4-octet sessions, sequence-only AS4_PATH draws None) and TestValidateAS4PathRejectsSetSegments, so the behavior is implemented and tested but the ledger's evidence omits it. Fix: tag TestRFC9774ReceiveAS4PathSetTreatAsWithdraw RFC9774-3-2 positive and negative (and TestValidateAS4PathRejectsSetSegments positive) with claims stating exactly what each body checks, record their discrimination with ./le rfc discriminate-record, then re-judge. Second finding: the comment in TestRFC9774ReceiveASSetAcceptedByOperator, "AS4_PATH reaches its validator only on a 2-octet session", is false at HEAD: the validator runs on every session and TestRFC9774ReceiveAS4PathSetTreatAsWithdraw asserts treat-as-withdraw on a 4-octet session; fix the comment, or add the 4-octet AS4_PATH row it implies is impossible. Discrimination: every recorded break is a panic in the producer (ASPathSetSegment, validateASPathPolicy), which proves the unit reaches the producer; the negatives discriminate by reading, since they assert exact nil or None. Units ran green at HEAD.
